item.content:encoded:
The 2026 Epic Users Group Meeting (UGM) just wrapped up, and we’ve seen two main sentiments pervading nearly every article, blog post, and opinion piece about the event: 1) excitement over Epic’s rapid AI automation capabilities, and 2) anxiety over how to afford and integrate those rapid changes. One notable tool is AI Charting, which drafts visit notes and suggests orders in real time, but several new features are arriving to summarize patient histories, speed up information retrieval, and take repetitive work off clinicians’ plates. Early results from Epic organizations are overall encouraging: less documentation burden, less after-hours work, and higher clinician satisfaction.

For healthcare IT teams, this is exciting and a little daunting. Every new AI feature brings a familiar question. Is our infrastructure secure and compliant enough to run this?

If you’re a VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) customer, the answer is yes. 

Getting over the hurdles

When a health system wants to adopt Epic’s AI tools, they face two separate hurdles. The first is the AI itself. Is it accurate? Is it fair? Does it actually help clinicians? Those are clinical and governance questions for the health system’s committees, informatics teams, and leadership. 

The second hurdle is the environment the AI runs in. Is the data encrypted? Is access controlled? Are there audit logs? Is it compliant with HIPAA? Can we prove it to regulators? This is where VCF does the heavy lifting.

Most of the delay in adopting new healthcare technology comes from the second hurdle, but VCF takes that hurdle off the critical path.

A pre-built, AI-ready foundation

Think of it like building a hospital wing for a new kind of surgery. You would not let clinicians start using it in an unrenovated, unequipped space. You would first need the right rooms, the right access controls, the right monitoring, and the right compliance sign-off. Only then does the new procedure become something safe to practice.

VCF is that pre-built wing. It arrives with security and compliance controls already in place: encryption that meets HIPAA standards out of the box, role-based access, network isolation between workloads, automated patching that does not require downtime, continuous compliance monitoring, and audit-ready reporting.

Faster, with lower risk

The pressure to adopt these tools quickly is putting strain on teams that are still trying to qualify and evaluate which tools will make the biggest impact. The necessary reviews can take a long time, but when the infrastructure underneath is already built to support those workloads and integrations securely, the team can focus on qualifying the AI tool’s fit and ROI. 

Risk in healthcare IT comes mostly from data exposure and operational disruption. VCF addresses both. Protected health information stays within the organization’s own environment, especially when Epic runs on-premises. Features such as live patching and redundant storage keep the EHR and its new AI features available even during maintenance, so the team doesn’t have to trade security for speed. They get both from the same foundation.

The Bottom Line

VCF takes the “is our infrastructure secure and does it support compliance enough to run AI?” question off the table so teams can focus on evaluating which AI capabilities are even worth using.

For VCF customers watching Epic’s AI roadmap, that is genuinely good news. The foundation is ready, so the conversation can move straight to the work that matters: getting these tools into the hands of clinicians safely and quickly.

P.S. If You’re Building Tools Yourself…

If part of your AI strategy includes building your own fit-for-purpose applications and GenAI tools, take a look at this four-part series, Hands-on Guide to Secure Private AI with Broadcom.

item.title: Automate DBaaS Operations on VCF with Agentic AI
item.dc:creator: vmwareblogs
item.description:
Database teams spend their days on a familiar set of tasks: provisioning, checking backups, staggering schedules so everything doesn’t hit the same S3 bucket at midnight on Saturday, patching aging instances, setting up replication for disaster recovery. None of these tasks is difficult in isolation. The problem is volume, and the way these tasks multiply … Continued

The post Automate DBaaS Operations on VCF with Agentic AI appeared first on VMware Blogs.
item.content:encoded:
Database teams spend their days on a familiar set of tasks: provisioning, checking backups, staggering schedules so everything doesn’t hit the same S3 bucket at midnight on Saturday, patching aging instances, setting up replication for disaster recovery. None of these tasks is difficult in isolation. The problem is volume, and the way these tasks multiply across PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQL Server estates running on private infrastructure.

Eric Gray from our VCF Tech Marketing team just published a demo that shows a different way to handle this work. In under twelve minutes, he walks through how an agentic AI CLI can manage operations in a VMware Data Services Manager environment. If you run databases on VCF, it’s worth your time.

What the Demo Covers

The setup is a DSM 9.1 environment with 14 active databases across PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQL Server. DSM is built on a Kubernetes API, so an AI agent can discover resources, inspect configurations, and take action through the same interface a human administrator would use. Eric starts with a read-only health sweep, then moves into changes.

The demo walks through four operations that database teams will recognize. A full health sweep surfaces version, build, license status, backup coverage, and upgrade availability across the entire fleet. Eric then staggers MySQL backup schedules so databases aren’t all hitting the same backup window, with the agent proposing a plan in plan mode before any change is applied. He configures PostgreSQL replication for disaster recovery, covering the replication slot, credential handoff, and secondary creation. He also upgrades a MySQL instance from an older version to the latest, with the agent confirming a valid backup and binlog archiving before patching.

Eric finishes by updating the data service policies that govern which database versions can be provisioned, tightening MySQL to version 8.4 only across both VCF Automation and native DSM policies.

Operational Insight: Why the Kubernetes API Makes This Work

DSM exposes a consistent Kubernetes API across every database engine it manages, which is what makes the agentic approach practical. An agent doesn’t need a separate integration for PostgreSQL, another for MySQL, and a third for SQL Server. It talks to one API, discovers custom resources, and acts on them.

For ops teams, the plan-mode workflow Eric demonstrates is the part to pay attention to. The agent proposes a change, you review it, and only then does it execute. That pattern keeps a human in the loop on anything that modifies the environment, which is the right default for production database operations. Read-only discovery runs without a checkpoint, while writes require explicit approval.

As teams bring more AI into their data center workflows, DSM’s API-first design means those agents have something structured to talk to. You work with the platform the way it was designed to be consumed, rather than scraping a UI or scripting around it.

Watch the Demo

If you manage databases on VCF, or you’re evaluating how AI fits into Day 2 operations, this demo is a clear, practical look at what’s possible today. Every operation maps to something you probably did manually this week.

item.title: Protecting Data Where It’s Most Vulnerable: How Broadcom and Intel Are Making Confidential Computing Real
item.dc:creator: vmwareblogs
item.description:
AI is only as trustworthy as the infrastructure it runs on. Organizations increasingly want to use AI with sensitive data, deploy workloads in regulated environments, and meet growing sovereignty requirements. Achieving those goals requires more than traditional security controls. It requires confidence that data, applications, and infrastructure can be trusted throughout the lifecycle of a … Continued

The post Protecting Data Where It’s Most Vulnerable: How Broadcom and Intel Are Making Confidential Computing Real appeared first on VMware Blogs.
item.content:encoded:
AI is only as trustworthy as the infrastructure it runs on. Organizations increasingly want to use AI with sensitive data, deploy workloads in regulated environments, and meet growing sovereignty requirements. Achieving those goals requires more than traditional security controls. It requires confidence that data, applications, and infrastructure can be trusted throughout the lifecycle of a workload.

Broadcom and Intel are helping organizations build that confidence through confidential computing capabilities integrated into VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF), creating a foundation for trusted AI, regulated workloads, and verifiable infrastructure security.

Why traditional security controls are no longer enough

Encrypting data at rest and in transit has become standard practice, and most enterprise security teams have those challenges well under control. The next challenge is protecting sensitive data while it is actively being processed. As organizations increasingly use AI to analyze proprietary information, customer data, and other business-critical assets, they need greater assurance that workloads remain protected during execution, not just while data is stored or transmitted. Confidential computing addresses this challenge, and it’s what Broadcom and Intel have been co-engineering into VMware Cloud Foundation across the 9.x release cycle.

The importance of protecting data in use has grown as AI adoption accelerates and regulatory expectations evolve. An inference workload processing financial records, patient data, or proprietary models remains exposed throughout execution. At the same time, organizations in highly regulated sectors such as financial services, healthcare, and government are increasingly being asked to demonstrate how sensitive data is protected while it is being processed, not simply how it is stored or moved.

The Security Foundation We Established jointly in VCF 9

Across VCF 9.0 and VCF 9.1, both Broadcom and Intel have been partnering to bring  confidential computing capabilities into VCF as a production-ready platform feature. Broadcom’s platform contributions included bringing confidential computing in as a generally available feature for the first time in VCF 9.1, supporting Intel TDX along with Quickboot support.  TPM 2.0 and vTPM integration established hardware roots of trust for every workload on the platform. Live Patching for TPM-enabled ESX hosts now applies security patches to up to 80% of CVEs with no VM evacuation, shrinking the window between vulnerability disclosure and a patched production host from weeks to hours. Continuous compliance enforcement keeps the security posture verifiable in real time rather than reconstructed before an audit.

Intel’s contribution starts at the lower layers of  VCF’s infrastructure stack and in the silicon itself. Intel Trust Domain Extensions (TDX), available on Intel Xeon 5 and newer processors, create hardware-isolated Trust Domains where individual VMs run with encrypted memory that the hypervisor cannot inspect. Intel QuickAssist Technology (QAT) accelerates cryptographic operations helping support  encrypted vMotion with minimal impact on CPU resources.

Intel is responsible for the silicon trust layer and Broadcom is responsible for the operational trust layer. Together they create an end-to-end chain of trust, backed by attestation, from the CPU through the hypervisor to the workload. The real value lies in the joint engineering and validation across the stack.  While TDX originates in silicon, delivering it as a production ready capability requires supported firmware, managed by VCF, to function as a platform feature customers can ship to production. Customers do not need to validate or troubleshoot the interaction between TDX firmware  and the ESX hypervisor themselves. That integration work has been done and validated jointly.

Delivering confidential computing at scale

Confidential VMs in VCF 9.1 run using the same operational model as standard VMs, with the same lifecycle management, compliance tooling, and processes. There’s no separate infrastructure footprint and no specialized expertise required to deploy a workload into a TEE. Organizations already running VCF on Intel Xeon 6 or Xeon 5 processors can enable confidential computing on existing  infrastructure.

For AI workloads, sensitive inference pipelines run inside hardware-isolated TEEs where data, models, and computations remain protected during execution . For security teams, hardware attestation reduces the compensating controls needed to satisfy auditors. For infrastructure teams, the operational model doesn’t change.

Looking ahead

As organizations deploy increasingly sensitive AI workloads and operate across more complex regulatory and sovereignty environments, trust in the execution environment is becoming as important as trust in the data itself. Confidential computing is evolving from a specialized security capability into a foundational layer for trusted AI, regulated workloads, and verifiable cloud infrastructure.

Broadcom and Intel continue to work together to simplify the adoption of confidential computing and bring hardware-rooted trust into mainstream enterprise operations. By combining Intel’s silicon-based security innovations with VMware Cloud Foundation’s operational capabilities, organizations can establish a verifiable chain of trust that extends from infrastructure to workload.

Getting started

Confidential Computing in VCF 9.1 is available today for organizations running sensitive AI, business-critical, or regulated workloads. Customers already running VMware Cloud Foundation from Intel Xeon 5 processors can evaluate Confidential Computing using existing infrastructure and operational processes. Broadcom account teams can help identify suitable workloads and provide access to joint Intel and Broadcom reference architectures and deployment guidance.

The post At VMware Explore 2026: Future-Proofing Enterprise AI with a Flexible Model Strategy appeared first on VMware Blogs.
item.content:encoded:
Choices in commercial, open-weight, and open source models have dramatically expanded over the past month. As a result, I’m continuing to see traction in organizations shaping their AI strategies around a hybrid approach, where they make use of our AI Gateway to connect users, agents, and application services to both cloud and on-premises models. Reasons for this approach often range from privacy, control, compliance, and latency requirements to tokenomics considerations. 

While all of this may sound great in theory, the adoption friction I often encounter is with organizations struggling with how to get started. This is why I’m looking forward to leading a panel discussion that will go deep into both the ecosystem and practical use cases at VMware Explore in just over a week. 

The panel session – Future-Proofing Enterprise AI: The Imperative of a Flexible AI Model Strategy for Your Infrastructure – will include leaders who are shaping the AI ecosystem: Alex Chen, Vice President at Alibaba Cloud Intelligence Group, Ben McCormack, Principle Software Engineer at Google, and Brett Tanzer, Vice President, Azure Solutions at Microsoft. 

Together, we’ll explore what it takes to make the most of models in the private cloud and with frontier model providers. Key areas that we will cover include:

  • Verticalization and specialization – Hear how leading model providers and innovating in frontier models, mixture of experts (MoE) models, and specialized small language models (SLMs). 
  • Choice – Learn how to think holistically across the ecosystem of choices to apply the right model to the right use case. 
  • Data sovereignty and control – Gain additional perspective on approaches to ensure that compliance, privacy and control mandates are satisfied. 
  • Optimized spending – Balance model performance, speed, accuracy, and specialization with predictable token costs. 
  • What the future holds – Our panelists will offer insights into what to expect in generative AI in the coming years. 

This session is sure to provide key data points to better prepare you to make informed decisions in the fast moving AI market. In addition, ample time will be left for you to ask the panelists about your most pressing concerns. 

Save your spot at the session. I look forward to seeing you there!

item.dc:creator: som chandra
item.description:
Executive Series • Modern Private Cloud Blueprint The cloud-native revolution is no longer a distant projection—it is the reality of modern enterprise technology. Across the globe, massive financial institutions, global retailers, and national-scale enterprises are reaching a critical crossroads: how to aggressively scale modern applications while maintaining the stability and compliance of mission-critical legacy systems. … Continued

The post Bridging the IT Chasm: A Strategic Blueprint for Platform Engineering 2.0 appeared first on VMware Blogs.
item.content:encoded:
Executive Series • Modern Private Cloud Blueprint

The cloud-native revolution is no longer a distant projection—it is the reality of modern enterprise technology. Across the globe, massive financial institutions, global retailers, and national-scale enterprises are reaching a critical crossroads: how to aggressively scale modern applications while maintaining the stability and compliance of mission-critical legacy systems.

Furthermore, as explored in the recent Broadcom insights regarding Frontier AI Security Models, the enterprise threat landscape is evolving at a breakneck pace. The rise of AI-driven threat actors means that vulnerability management has fundamentally shifted from traditional triage precision to a mandate of absolute patching velocity. In this hyper-accelerated risk environment, running disconnected infrastructure or relying on siloed automation across critical enterprise applications is no longer just an operational bottleneck; it is an unacceptable security liability.

To stay ahead, senior leaders must transition away from fragmented infrastructure toolsets toward a unified architecture. By pairing VMware vSphere Kubernetes Service (VKS)—the core container runtime native to VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF)—with Broadcom’s Automic Automation, strategic IT leaders can bridge the gap between cloud-native speed and legacy operational stability. This architecture effectively eradicates manual operational friction during critical security events. Automic Automation provides the deterministic orchestration required for machine-speed remediation across complex, multi-generational digital estates and mission-critical tasks.

The Enterprise Mandate: Crushing the ‘Kubernetes Tax’

Organizations migrating monolithic apps to modern containerized microservices are grappling with infrastructure sprawl and dual-vendor licensing penalties. Running separate Kubernetes management platforms on top of the hypervisor layer creates a compounding cost model that degrades ROI.

By leveraging VMware VKS with Automic Automation, executives can unlock significant TCO savings compared to public clouds and legacy 3-tier architectures.  VKS is an inherent entitlement within the VCF subscription—meaning organizations deploy CNCF-certified Kubernetes at zero extra licensing cost provided customers have an active VCF subscription. Layering Automic Automation over VCF helps increase business velocity, reducing unplanned downtime and ensuring that high-value business processes are fully digitized and resilient. In modern commercial conversations, clients are laser-focused on maximizing the utilization of their VCF per-core subscriptions. This approach shifts the conversation from a data center line-item to an agile application delivery play.

The Ecosystem Synergy: A Unified Broadcom Stack

For our global systems integrators and ecosystem partners, the Automic-VKS-VCF validation eliminates the multi-vendor integration friction that routinely stalls digital transformation initiatives. Instead of stitching together fragmented open-source orchestration tools, legacy schedulers, and public cloud container services, partners can now offer a singular, hardened stack from Broadcom. This architecture enables partners to build robust, repeatable Cloud-Native Migration practices that modernize client estates without requiring a risky, ground-up hypervisor replacement.

Under the Hood: Declarative Orchestration Meets Hypervisor-Native K8s

Architecturally, the integration points between Automic Automation and VKS represent a massive leap forward for platform engineers. VKS embeds Kubernetes directly into the vSphere hypervisor, utilizing the Supervisor layer to control cluster life cycles via the Cluster API.

Automic acts as the central nervous system across this fabric, ensuring that core business data moving through legacy enterprise platforms like SAP can automatically trigger, track, and depend on containerized microservices running natively on VKS clusters.

Zero-Trust Network Micro-segmentation: Automated workflows are isolated at the transport layer via VMware NSX. Benefiting from VKS’ native integration with VMware NSX, any containerized job triggered by Automic Automation automatically adheres to the strict zero-trust network micro-segmentation and lateral security policies defined at the infrastructure layer.

Enterprise-Class Storage & Data Persistence: Stateful automated jobs running in VKS clusters leverage the native vSAN CSI driver, helping guarantee dynamic volume provisioning with enterprise-grade SLA enforcement.

Platform Engineering 2.0: Lowering the Developer Cognitive Burden

Product Managers of internal IT platforms know that forcing developers to become Kubernetes experts or infrastructure specialists degrades velocity. The goal of Platform Engineering is to create a “Golden Path”—a frictionless, self-service experience.

Automic Automation coupled with VKS serves as the definitive backend for an Internal Developer Platform (IDP). By encapsulating complex, multi-system workflows into standardized, policy-as-code blueprints within VCF Automation, developers can provision namespaces, trigger containerized application testing, and connect to legacy databases with a single API call or click. The platform team maintains governance via built-in VKS guardrails, while the application teams get the cloud-like agility they demand.

Introducing the Series: Top 3 Strategic Pillars for the Modern Enterprise

This blog marks the first in a refined three-part series where we will explore the immense technical and financial value of this combined Broadcom ecosystem. In the coming weeks, we will publish a detailed deep-dive blog for each of the three foundational pillars this blueprint solves for our strategic customers:

  1. Unifying the Multi-Generational IT Chasm: We will explore how Automic Automation acts as the end-to-end service orchestration platform, seamlessly triggering containerized microservices running natively on VKS from legacy core systems (mainframes, SAP), entirely eliminating manual handoffs.
  2. Maximizing Entitlements and Eradicating the Kubernetes Tax: We will detail how VKS simplifies Day-2 operations natively within vSphere, and how Automic’s Automation-as-Code slashes administrative overhead, delivering a unified private cloud that drastically reduces TCO compared to fragmented public cloud stacks.
  3. Predictive SLA Management and Governed Zero-Trust Workflows: Minutes of downtime mean lost revenue. We will unpack how Automic Automation enforces predictive SLA management and how VKS delivers FIPS-compliant, isolated environments enforced by role-based automation policies from the infrastructure to the application layer.

Key Takeaway

Automic Automation manages the end-to-end lifecycle of mission-critical jobs—ERP, SCM, CRM etc. across both traditional VMs and modern VKS container pods on VCF, removing legacy constraints that slow downcloud-native application delivery.

Strategic Next Steps

The frontier is no longer about who can reach the cloud first—it is about who can command it with the most precision and defend it with the greatest velocity. Managing Kubernetes with the control of a private cloud, orchestrated by the industry’s most powerful automation engine, prepares your team to architect your future growth securely.

To dive deeper into the technical validation, architectural topology maps, and containerized deployment models, read the official Broadcom reference document: Automic Automation on vSphere Kubernetes Service within VMware Cloud Foundation.

A new session just landed in the VMware Explore 2026 Content Catalog, and it’s worth prioritizing. J.R. Storment, Executive Director of the FinOps Foundation and Tokenomics Foundation, will join Broadcom experts for a conversation about tokenomics and connecting AI investments to business and IT value. 

Organizations are spending tremendous amounts of money on infrastructure to become AI-savvy. But how do you determine whether that spend is producing real value, and how do you navigate it across the complexity of the AI stack: your cloud providers, your on-prem estates, and everything in between? 

Tokenomics is often viewed as a mere cost metric for hyperscalers or frontier LLMs. This session explains how it can be a strategic tool for measuring and articulating business outcomes. 

You’ll learn how to:

  • Connect AI investments to value. Measure and prove return on infrastructure investment across hybrid cloud estates.
  • Align with open industry standards. Hear first-hand from the head of the Tokenomics Foundation about vendor-neutral benchmarks for AI economics. (The foundation was launched in August 2026 by the Linux Foundation, with Broadcom as a founding member.)
  • Scale sustainably fast. Private AI brings models directly to your data, enabling you to become AI-first in a cost-effective, sustainable way.

VI Admins are becoming AI Admins. Learn how to bridge the gap between your infrastructure team and business on AI usage.

In July, AWS announced support for VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) 9.0 and 9.1 on Amazon Elastic VMware Service (EVS), giving customers the ability to run VCF 9.x directly in their Amazon VPC on EC2 bare-metal infrastructure. At VMware Explore 2026, we’re bringing other major hyperscalers together to share the latest on their VCF 9.1 readiness and hybrid deployment options.

The session “Accelerate VCF 9 Upgrade with Hyperscaler Solutions for Hybrid Deployments” will feature a roundtable with representatives from leading hyperscalers. You’ll get an inside look at their VCF 9.1 roadmaps, discuss hybrid deployment options, and have the opportunity to ask your specific deployment questions directly to the experts.

VCF License Portability

At the heart of this discussion is the enterprise value of VCF license portability. With eligible subscription entitlements, you can move VMware workloads to hyperscalers with no refactoring. You can also transfer the remaining value of your VCF subscription to a hyperscaler and move entitlements back and forth as your business requirements evolve.

That flexibility lets you choose where workloads run as your business needs change, using familiar VMware tooling and skillsets while picking up new cloud capabilities. 

If you’re planning a VCF 9 upgrade, evaluating hybrid deployment options, or have questions for the hyperscalers themselves, reserve your spot through the Explore Content Catalog.

item.content:encoded:
VMware Explore provides a wonderful venue for security-minded VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) users to get direct access to VCF security experts, test-drive security capabilities in Hands-on Labs (HOLs), and master the blueprints for safeguarding enterprise workloads against AI-powered threats. Supercharge your skills and learn about the latest capabilities at VMware Explore 2026 in Las Vegas, August 31 – September 3. Here are the key security and compliance sessions and activities you shouldn’t miss.

Breakout Sessions

These breakout sessions focus on securing VCF itself. You’ll walk away with practical, real-world perspectives on the AI threat landscape and how teams are staying ahead of it using VCF Security capabilities.

Hands-on Labs

If you learn best by doing, our Expert-led Workshops are a must. Developed and led by the very subject-matter experts (SMEs) who built the labs, these interactive sessions give you access to a live environment where you can explore VCF 9.1 capabilities firsthand. Pro tip: these fill up fast, but we’ll have onsite standby seats available for drop-ins. 

Prefer to set your own pace? The same labs are available on-demand in our Self-paced Labs area, no registration required. Our product SMEs are stationed right in the room, ready to answer your deepest technical questions as you work through each scenario. It’s hands-on VCF Security learning, on your terms.

Meet the Expert Roundtables

Meet the Expert Roundtables offer small-group discussions with subject-matter experts. They are a great opportunity to ask your most pressing questions and get answers straight from the experts.

Quick Talks

Demonstrations

Explore all the demo booths at the Hub. In particular, visit the “Fortify Your Private Cloud against AI-Driven Threats” booth to learn about how VCF can protect customers from attacks with frontier AI, key features such as ESX Live Patching and vSAN Data Protection. 

Meetings

Please contact your Broadcom sales account team to arrange in-depth, onsite meetings if you are interested in the following meeting topics!

  • Defending Against AI-Powered Threats with VCF 9.1
  • VCF Security Assessment and Recommendations for Defending Against Frontier AI Exploits
